name: On-site solar plus battery storage for data centres
applications: Firming part of a campus load behind the meter
Reducing peak demand charges and supporting grid services
principle: Solar plus storage behind the meter changes the profile of a campus's grid draw without changing the load: the array produces while the sun is up, the battery shifts that energy to evening peaks and can also provide demand response. It is not a substitute for utility capacity, because a data centre load runs continuously and a solar array's capacity factor is a fraction of its nameplate - which is why the IEA sees renewables meeting only about half of the additional demand, with gas and coal behind them.

process_steps.name: Inverters convert to AC at the site distribution voltage
Site switchboard couples solar, battery and grid
Battery charges, discharges and provides grid services

performance.metric: share of additional data centre demand met by renewables over five years
performance.basis: IEA: over five years renewables meet nearly half of the additional data centre demand, followed by gas and coal; solar and wind are the renewable sources in that mix.

source.note: IEA, Energy and AI, Energy supply for AI, read 2026-11-14

advantages: Reduces grid import and scope-2 emissions without changing the IT load
Battery can earn demand-response and frequency-service revenue
limitations: Solar capacity factor is far below the round-the-clock load, so it displaces energy rather than capacity
Land or roof area is the binding constraint at campus scale
Battery fire code, insurance and permitting add cost and time
